page: Microsoft Azure E4_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Ev4 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The configuration provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AES cryptography, and Intel virtualization technology.

This instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include any local storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, meaning all storage requirements must be fulfilled via external network-attached block storage.

Benchmark results indicate that the E4_v4 exhibits modest compute capabilities. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as measured by stress-ng and PassMark, falls into the lower 25th percentile. Memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations also rank in the bottom tier, though Geekbench single-core and PassMark memory scores achieve average performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is positioned as a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-performance compute or local NVMe storage, trading raw processing speed for a larger memory footprint.

The E4_v4 is suited for memory-intensive applications with moderate CPU demands. Appropriate workloads include caching layers, relational databases with small-to-medium datasets, lightweight enterprise applications, and memory-bound data processing tasks that fit within its 32.0 GB RAM capacity.
